explainer.lead: This entry covers the practical quantisation ecosystem: GPTQ and AWQ for GPU-served 4-bit models, GGUF as the llama.cpp format for CPU and edge use, bitsandbytes for on-the-fly 8/4-bit loading, and FP8 for modern-accelerator serving. Choice among them depends on hardware and stack.

tiers.eli5: These are different ways of squeezing a big model into less memory, and which one you use depends on the computer you run it on.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick a quantisation format to match their hardware and serving stack: GPTQ or AWQ on GPUs, GGUF on CPU and edge devices, bitsandbytes for on-the-fly loading, FP8 on modern accelerators. A pitfall is that the right choice depends on the hardware and stack, so formats are not interchangeable.

explainer.example: A team serving a 4-bit model on GPUs uses GPTQ or AWQ, while a team running the same model on edge devices uses GGUF with llama.cpp.
